title: TrustJev: Separating Policy Authority from Untrusted Evidence in LLM-Based Decisions
abstract: arXiv:2610.34826v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decision models enable software to select from predefined actions using natural language inputs. However, the external evidence that supplies facts for these decisions may also contain instructions that attempt to override the application's policy. We propose TrustJev, a framework combining protected policy scoring with bounded evidence corrections. A single Transformer backbone computes policy scores and a correction budget from trusted policy and candidates, then bounds evidence corrections by that budget. Paired supervision encourages stable predictions under instruction insertions that preserve task facts and changed preferences when edits change the correct answer. Authority supervision accommodates evidence when the policy alone cannot determine the decision. We evaluate a 0.6B implementation against 14 baselines on three datasets covering authentication, instruction hierarchy, and executable authorization rules. TrustJev achieves

translated_abstract: 决策模型使软件能够根据自然语言输入从预定义动作中进行选择。然而，为这些决策提供事实依据的外部证据也可能包含试图覆盖应用程序策略的指令。我们提出了TrustJev，一个将受保护的策略评分与有界证据修正相结合的框架。单一Transformer骨干网络从可信策略和候选选项中计算策略评分与修正预算，然后以该预算约束证据修正。成对监督机制鼓励在保留任务事实的指令插入下保持预测稳定，并在编辑改变正确答案时相应调整偏好。权威监督机制则允许在策略本身无法确定决策时纳入证据。我们在涵盖身份验证、指令层级和可执行授权规则的三个数据集上，将0.6B参数规模的实现与14个基线方法进行了评估。TrustJev取得了
tldr: TrustJev框架通过单一Transformer骨干网络同时计算受保护的策略评分和证据修正预算，将决策权威保留在可信策略侧，并以预算约束来自不可信外部证据的修正幅度，从而有效抵御证据中的指令注入攻击。
en_tdlr: TrustJev is a framework that uses a single Transformer backbone to compute protected policy scores and a bounded correction budget, keeping decision authority with the trusted policy while constraining corrections from untrusted evidence to defend against instruction injection attacks.
